title: Seller's Property Disclosure Statement
description: Minnesota Statutes §§ 513.52-513.60 require sellers of residential real property to make a written disclosure to the prospective buyer before the parties sign a purchase agreement (Minn. Stat. § 513.55). The disclosure must include all material facts of which the seller is aware that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment of the property or any intended use the buyer has disclosed. The requirement may alternatively be satisfied by a qualified third-party inspection report (Minn. Stat. § 513.56), and may be waived only if the seller and buyer both agree to the waiver in writing (Minn. Stat. § 513.60). The seller must amend the disclosure if new adverse material facts arise before closing (Minn. Stat. § 513.58).

required_actions.note: Disclosure must be delivered in writing BEFORE the purchase agreement is signed. Waiver is valid only by written agreement of both seller and buyer per Minn. Stat. § 513.60; a third-party inspection report may substitute per Minn. Stat. § 513.56.

title: Well Disclosure Statement and Well Disclosure Certificate
description: Minnesota Statutes § 103I.235 (Ground Water Protection Act) requires that before signing an agreement to sell or transfer real property, the seller disclose in writing the location and status of all known wells on the property, or state that the seller knows of no wells. At conveyance, the county recorder or registrar of titles may not record the deed unless it contains a no-wells statement or is accompanied by a completed Well Disclosure Certificate (filed with the Minnesota Department of Health; statutory receipt fee of $54 collected at recording). Applies to deeds dated after October 31, 1990.

required_actions.note: Seller must disclose in writing, before the purchase agreement is signed, the legal description, county, and a map showing the location and status of each known well, or a statement that no wells are known.

Deed cannot be recorded without either a no-wells statement on the deed or an accompanying Well Disclosure Certificate (MDH form). A $54 fee is collected by the county recorder for receipt of the certificate.

title: Radon Disclosure (Minnesota Radon Awareness Act)
description: Minnesota Statutes § 144.496 (Minnesota Radon Awareness Act) requires that before signing an agreement to sell or transfer residential real property, the seller disclose in writing any knowledge of radon concentrations in the dwelling, including whether radon testing has occurred, the most current test records and reports, any mitigation or remediation performed, documentation of any installed radon mitigation system, and the statutory radon warning statement. The seller must also provide the buyer a copy of the Minnesota Department of Health publication 'Radon in Real Estate Transactions'. Effective for agreements executed on or after January 1, 2014.

required_actions.document: MDH publication 'Radon in Real Estate Transactions'

required_actions.note: Disclosure must include the statutory radon warning statement (Minn. Stat. § 144.496, subd. 4) and be delivered before the purchase agreement is signed. MSBA Real Property Form No. 24 is the customary disclosure instrument.

title: Subsurface Sewage Treatment System (Septic) Disclosure
description: Minnesota Statutes § 115.55, subd. 6 requires that before signing an agreement to sell or transfer real property, the seller disclose in writing how sewage generated at the property is managed, including whether the property is served by a subsurface sewage treatment system (SSTS), the system's location, and the seller's knowledge of its operating status and compliance. If the property is not connected to a municipal sewer, this disclosure is mandatory and is customarily delivered with the seller's property disclosure statement.

required_actions.note: Written disclosure of sewage treatment method, SSTS location, and known compliance status before the purchase agreement is signed.

title: Agency Relationship Disclosure at First Substantive Contact
description: Minnesota Statutes § 82.67 requires a real estate broker or salesperson, in a residential real property transaction, to provide the consumer with the statutory agency disclosure form at the first substantive contact. The form describes the available agency and facilitator relationship options, the licensee's role under each, and includes a signature line acknowledging receipt. Dual agency requires the informed written consent of both parties (Minn. Stat. § 82.67, subd. 2).

required_actions.note: Must be delivered at first substantive contact with the consumer. Dual agency permitted only with informed written consent of both buyer and seller.

metadata.note: Section 82.67 is the 2011 recodification of Minnesota's longstanding agency disclosure requirement in Chapter 82.

title: Licensed Closing Agent; Trust Funds; Wet-Funding Closing
description: Minnesota is a title/escrow closing state with wet funding: loan proceeds are disbursed at closing. Minnesota Statutes § 82.641 prohibits a person from acting as a real estate closing agent without a license, subject to statutory exemptions (licensed attorneys and their direct employees, direct employees of authorized title insurers or title insurance agents, and direct employees of a licensed broker using the broker's trust account). All funds received in connection with closing services must be held in a compliant trust account under Minn. Stat. § 82.75. Attorney presence at closing is not required.

required_actions.note: Verify the closing agent is licensed under Minn. Stat. § 82.641 or falls within a statutory exemption. Closing funds must be maintained in a trust account per Minn. Stat. § 82.75; disbursement occurs at closing (wet funding).

title: State Deed Tax and Electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value (eCRV)
description: Minnesota Statutes § 287.21 imposes a state deed tax, payable when the deed is presented for recording, of 0.33% (.0033) of the net consideration; a minimum tax of $1.65 applies when consideration is $3,000 or less. Hennepin and Ramsey Counties impose an additional .0001 environmental response fund tax. Minnesota Statutes § 272.115 requires that whenever real estate is sold for consideration exceeding $3,000 — by warranty deed, quitclaim deed, contract for deed, or any other method — an electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value (eCRV) be filed with the county when the deed or other conveyance document is presented for recording.

required_actions.note: 0.33% of net consideration (minimum $1.65 when consideration is $3,000 or less); customarily paid by the seller. Additional .0001 environmental response fund tax in Hennepin and Ramsey Counties.

required_actions.document: eCRV (electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value)
required_actions.note: Required for sales with consideration over $3,000; deed will not be processed for recording without it.
